operations.classification: open-work (NOT accepted). The old text ('Random, so the set is non-deterministic') was only half true and it hid two real divergences. Random here PERMUTES but does not change the set: `SuggestionsController` runs ONE query (`OrderBy = [(Random, Descending)]`, Recursive, mediaType/type, IsVirtualItem=false) and Ferrofin's handler is a line-for-line port, so at `limit >= |universe|` the answer is fully determined and parity_diff aligns Items by Path. The probe was the problem: `limit=10` sampled 10 of 552 at random and could never diff. It is now eight legs: seven pinned at a full limit (per type), where Random only permutes and the whole body IS diffed, plus one narrow startIndex/limit leg. That narrow leg is the one place a projection is applied — a page of 3 out of 500 Random-ordered rows draws a different triple per call on BOTH servers (measured: three consecutive calls, three different triples each side), so it compares StartIndex, TotalRecordCount and the page length only. Diffing its Items would pin this row red forever and destroy its ability to signal when the two real divergences below are fixed; the projection is scoped to that leg alone and nothing was added to parity_diff.VOLATILE. Two causes remain, BOTH owned by other rows and deliberately left visible here rather than filtered out of the probe: (1) ITEM UNIVERSE — Ferrofin's recursive user-root universe has no MusicArtist, Folder, TvChannel or UserView rows (F 552 vs J 561 unfiltered; per type F 0 vs J 3/3/2/1), the same parentless-by-name/TopParentId cause as GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar; detector `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&limit=100000`, which shows the identical 9-row delta, so it is not this handler's bug. (2) PER-ITEM DTO FIELDS — MediaSources[].Name/Bitrate, MediaStreams[].BitRate (a constant 192000 offset), LocalizedLanguage, Level/IsAVC/Width/Height: the same set already classified on GET /Items/{itemId} as independent-probe noise, inherited here because Suggestions returns full item DTOs. Narrowing the compare to hide either would be the dishonest green; the row stays red until they are fixed on their own rows. The multi-leg probe no longer skips a leg whose servers disagree on status: a status divergence (or a body that is not 200-with-JSON on both sides) is recorded as a mismatch, which is the whole point of keeping the type=MusicArtist and type=TvChannel legs. UNIVERSE GAP, re-measured 2026-08-29 and WIDER than first written: LiveTvProgram belongs on the missing-kind list too — `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=LiveTvProgram` returns 338 rows on Jellyfin and 0 on Ferrofin, while `/LiveTv/Programs` returns the guide on both (F 19200, J 338). The knock-on is visible on a THIRD row: GET /Genres is red only because Jellyfin's genre list carries `News`, the XMLTV guide's programme genre, which Ferrofin's genre list cannot see for the same reason. One fix (give the by-name/programme rows a TopParentId so `scope_to_user_libraries` stops filtering them out) closes /Artists Similar, these Suggestions legs and the /Genres row together; it changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it is its own change WITH the perf gate.
